For a transmon with anharmonicity $\chi$, the dominant error in an X-pi pulse comes from the leakage to the $|2\rangle$ state. This leakage is proportional to the integral of the pulse envelope squared, weighted by the anharmonicity and the pulse shape. Specifically, the off-resonant drive to the $|1\rangle \to |2\rangle$ transition (detuning $\chi$) creates a population in $|2\rangle$.

The standard DRAG condition is that the Q-component should be proportional to the derivative of the I-component, with a coefficient $\sigma_{DRAG} = \frac{|\chi|}{2 \Omega_{max}}$.

def hamiltonian(detuning, scale, I, Q):
    """Build the 3x3 Hamiltonian."""

    For efficiency, we evolve the state vector directly using the Lindblad equation

    vec(dρ/dt) = -i (H ⊗ I - I ⊗ H†) vec(ρ) + Σ_k (L_k ⊗ L_k*) vec(ρ) - 0.5 Σ_k (L_k†L_k ⊗ I + I ⊗ L_k†L_k) vec(ρ)

    H_term = -1j * (np.kron(H, np.eye(dim)) - np.kron(np.eye(dim), H.conj().T))

        Ldag = L.conj().T
        LdagL = Ldag @ L
